newsitem.title: UK: Report sees rising rental values in UK property.
newsitem.headline: Report sees rising rental values in UK property.

text.p: Rental values in the UK property market are rising, with the year-on-year total return on property exceeding 10 percent as at the end of February, a report said on Monday.
According to property consultants Richard Ellis, the February figure is the first time total returns have been more than 10 percent since January 1995.
"In all markets rental values are now rising. We expect this trend to continue over the coming months," said Angus McIntosh, director of research at Richard Ellis.
McIntosh said political events in the next few weeks "are unlikely to disturb the improving trend in the property investment market". The ruling Conservative government must call an election by May.

The Richard Ellis monthly index, based on the performance of 412 properties across the UK, found the return on all property stood at 10.1 percent, on offices 10.2 percent, on industrial property 11.2 percent, in-town shops 8.8 percent and retail warehouses 16.4 percent.

McIntosh said that although the initial rental income yield stood at 8.5 percent and had not changed significantly in recent months, it was "reassuring to see that capital values are beginning top increase in all four sectors".
